title: Design System: Goodput Festival of Code

display.purpose: The cover title, fitted to the measure. The same face sets roundel numerals, entrant names, the fat event line and the notice heading on clamps between ramp values.

headline.purpose: The one condensed-slab line that opens every page; the coupon and the cover date use the same face between ramp endpoints.

title.purpose: Condensed slab for driver names and the event names in the order of events.

script.purpose: Two overlines crossing a headline's baseline; carries a ground-colour stroke.

figure.purpose: --t-figure. The forecast figure (italic, tabular) and the defined word (poster face).

stamp.purpose: --t-stamp. Rubber-stamp capitals; the 24px floor for vermilion on yellow.

lede-l.purpose: --t-lede-l. Foreword opening, address, notice text; also the Order of events heading in label capitals.

lede.purpose: --t-lede. The opening paragraph of a page, in narrow columns.

body.purpose: --t-body. Running text in the Modern face.

small.purpose: --t-small. Table values and the definition; body size under 700px.

caption.purpose: --t-caption. Italic folios, captions, footnotes and hints in the page's soft screened colour.

label-l.purpose: --t-label-l. Buttons, block titles, the venue line.

label.purpose: --t-label. Table terms, running head, form labels; tracked .13em to .16em.

label-s.purpose: --t-label-s. The Detach here tab and the running-head name on phones.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The only easing curve; every hover, press and entrance.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Colour changes on buttons and links (.2s on event names); press is .12s, arrow advance .25s.

motion.name: register
motion.purpose: Cover plates and title slide into register from up to 26px away, once, on load.

motion.name: seal-in
motion.purpose: The price seal lands from 1.5 scale after the plates are home; the off-the-clock stamp uses the same landing in .22s.

motion.name: plate-life
motion.value: wheels .5s x 9, jolt .34s x 13, streak .9s x 5, flutter .42s x 11, dust 1.1s x 4
motion.purpose: The cover plate moves while it prints, then settles into a still print; a pointer over it restarts the loops.

motion.name: chronometric-tick
motion.purpose: The dial needle steps to its value; it never sweeps. Reduced motion jumps straight there.

rules.name: leader
rules.purpose: Dot leaders (60 to 70% strength) and the forecast baseline.

rules.name: oxford
rules.purpose: Section breaks; a lone 5px rule heads lists and definitions.

rules.name: frame
rules.purpose: Forecast box and plan; stamp; notice and grid box.

rules.name: perforation
rules.purpose: The coupon's tear line and the grid's centre line.

screens.name: hatch
screens.purpose: Body shading on the car and portraits.

screens.name: misregister
screens.purpose: Resting offset of the colour passes; red also multiplies.

screens.name: grain
screens.purpose: Paper tooth: dark flecks on buff and yellow, light flecks on green.

shared.menuContract: details.treatments[data-treatments] > summary (.treatments__label, .treatments__current, .treatments__chev) + ul.treatments__menu > li > a[aria-current] (strong, span)

rules.name: The Separate Worlds Rule
rules.body: A treatment owns its folder, its stylesheet, its script, its fonts folder and its portraits. No typeface, colour token or component style crosses from one treatment to another; a face used by one is not available to the other two.

rules.name: The Behaviour Only Rule
rules.body: Files under `docs/assets/js/` that all three load carry behaviour and settings only. They set no styles, inject no markup and name no colours, so each treatment draws the shared menu and states in its own vocabulary.

rules.name: The Same Facts Rule
rules.body: All three say the same things: the same dates, venue, four drivers and racing numbers, three customers, the record left unposted, the same closed and open states. A fact changed on one is changed on all three.

tower.name: The Timekeepers' Tower
tower.reviewStatus: finish review passed (ship) after one fix round

fonts.num: Big Shoulders Display, Arial Narrow, sans-serif

motion.name: hang
motion.value: .62s date tiles, delays .1s to .78s; .5s forecast tiles, 90ms stagger

tower.signature: Hang your forecast: the figure is hung tile by tile on the visitor's row of seven hooks.

rules.name: The Painted or Paper Rule
rules.body: What is painted on a board is set in the signwriter's faces. What is typed or pencilled is always on paper: the ledger sheet or a slip pinned to a board. The typewriter and the pencil never appear directly on paint.

rules.name: The One Module Rule
rules.body: Boards, tiles, gaps and lettering painted at board scale are sized in modules, so the tower keeps its proportions at every width.

rules.name: The Bare Hooks Rule
rules.body: A value that does not exist yet is shown as empty hooks and the words "to be posted". No figure, dash or zero stands in for it.

rules.name: The Red on Cream Rule
rules.body: Red appears on cream, or as the whole warning board. It is never laid on yellow or green.

donts: Don't set small tiles in a grid of metrics; tiles are few and large.
Don't fade, slide or loop anything; a tile drops onto its hooks once.
Don't put typed or pencilled text straight onto a board.
Don't use gradients, shadows or gloss highlights; the paint is flat and tone is one hatch.
Don't borrow the Programme's or the Lap Chart's faces, inks or furniture.

lap-chart.name: The Hand-Inked Lap Chart

motion.name: ink
motion.value: 3.4s linear after .35s, one stroke along a mask

lap-chart.signature: Pencil in a forecast: inked as a gold coil, then unrolled onto twelve ruled rows of exactly the same length, 1,000 tokens per second to the row.

rules.name: The One Question, One Chart Rule
rules.body: Each plate asks one question and answers it with one drawing whose form belongs to that question. No chart form is reused as a template.

rules.name: The Counted or Blank Rule
rules.body: A length drawn to scale was counted. Anything not yet known is drawn blank, or to no scale and labelled so. No figure appears that was not counted or entered by the visitor.

rules.name: The Drawn Waver Rule
rules.body: The hand is in the geometry, produced by the build script. No blur, displacement or roughening filter is applied, and measured drawings are ruled true.

rules.name: The Generated Page Rule
rules.body: The page is built from the template and the build script. A change is made there and rebuilt, never in the generated file.

donts: Don't draw axes-and-cards analytics, gauges or dashboards.
Don't rank the customers or size anything by a number nobody measured.
Don't use gradients, shadows or filters; inks are flat and saturated inside an ink keyline.
Don't set the drafting hand in lower case, or prose in it.
Don't borrow the Programme's or the Tower's faces, inks or furniture.

narrative.overview:
The site is the souvenir programme of a 1930s-50s race meeting, read page by page. Each section is a printed page in one stock or one ink: a chrome-yellow cover, buff text pages, a racing-green plate, a salmon insert, a yellow tear-off coupon, a black colophon. Nothing is a card floating on a background; the page itself is the object, edge to edge, and it changes colour when you turn it.

Everything on it is made the way a jobbing printer would have made it. Four inks, flat. Tone comes from dot screens and hatching, never from blends. The passes sit slightly out of register and the vermilion overprints what lies beneath it. Five typefaces each have one job and are never swapped. The furniture is the furniture of a programme: dot-leader entry tables, Oxford rules, number roundels, rubber stamps, a price seal, a perforation line with scissors. Every piece of that furniture carries a real fact about the event.

The density is that of print: very large bill lines set to fill their measure, then quiet book-weight text in narrow columns beside them. Motion belongs to the press and the instrument: plates slide into register once, a chronometric needle steps rather than sweeps, wheels turn and then settle into print.
keyCharacteristics: Four inks (chrome yellow, racing green, vermilion, ink black) on buff stock, plus one salmon insert stock. No other colour exists.
Flat shapes only: no gradients, no shadows, no blur. Depth is overprint, knockout and misregistration.
Square corners on every box; circles only where the period object is round (roundels, seals, dials).
Five single-weight voices: fat poster capitals, tracked label capitals, a tall condensed slab, a Modern text face, one brush script.
Full-bleed pages that change stock, each closed by an italic folio ("Page three").
Bill lines are fitted to the column width by script; they wrap on phones.
Paper tooth: a fine noise grain over buff, yellow and green pages.

rules.name: The Four Inks Rule
rules.body: Every colour on a page is one of the four inks or one of the two stocks. A lighter tone is made with a dot screen, a hatch, or the two "soft" screened values, never with a new colour, an alpha wash over a photograph, or a gradient.

rules.name: The Whole Page Rule
rules.body: An ink that owns a page owns it edge to edge. Yellow, green and salmon are never used as tinted panels inside a buff page.

rules.name: The Vermilion Size Rule
rules.body: Vermilion on chrome yellow measures about 3.9:1, so it is set only at display sizes (24px and up): the title, the script, the stamp. Small text on yellow is ink black. Vermilion on buff (about 4.6:1) may go down to heading sizes.

rules.name: The Five Voices Rule
rules.body: Each face has one job. Poster capitals for names and numbers, the slab for bill lines, label capitals for anything a clerk would stamp or rule, the Modern for anything read as a sentence, the script for a flourish across a headline. Do not set a sentence in the label face or a label in the text face.

rules.name: The Fitted Line Rule
rules.body: A bill line marked for fitting is sized by script to fill its column on one line (less 2px), after fonts load and on resize. Under 700px the fitted event names are released to wrap at a fixed clamp. Stars between names are drawn marks that ride the line's measure.

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: A static size is one of the ten ramp steps. A fluid size is one of the four fluid roles, or a clamp whose two ends are both values on the ramp. A new size is a new step added to the ramp on purpose, never a one-off.

rules.name: The Drawn Lettering Rule
rules.body: Lettering inside a plate (seal, scrutineer's stamp, the car's number, dial, plan) is part of the drawing: it is sized as an attribute on the drawn text in the drawing's own units and scales with the plate, at one size for every width. It is not on the page ramp and is never sized from the stylesheet.

rules.name: The Whole Name Rule
rules.body: The script crosses a headline at its baseline only, so every letter of the headline stays legible.

rules.name: The Flat Ink Rule
rules.body: If a surface needs to look lifted, darker or lit, it is drawn that way with a screen, a hatch, a keyline or a second pass out of register. Shadows and gradients are not in this system.

rules.name: The Keyline Rule
rules.body: Where one ink would be lost against another (the vermilion needle on the black dial, the script over a headline), it gets a thin stroke in the ground colour painted beneath the fill, not a glow.

dos: Do give each new page one stock or ink, full bleed, with the paper grain on buff, yellow and green, and close it with an italic folio.
Do open a page with a single bill line in the condensed slab, then set the facts beneath it in narrow columns on the twelve-column sheet (1320px cap).
Do put tabular facts in a race card: label capitals, dot leader, value ranged right, 1.5px rules.
Do make tone with dot screens (5px grid at 45 degrees), hatching and knockouts, and let passes sit a pixel or two out of register.
Do keep vermilion on yellow to 24px and larger; use ink black for anything smaller on yellow.
Do take every type size from the ramp, and size lettering inside a plate in the drawing itself.
Do keep every box square and every rule in the page's text colour, at 1.5px, 2px, 3px, 5px or 6px.
Do use the yellow focus ring on green and black grounds and the ink ring on yellow, buff and salmon.
Do let a programme device carry a real fact (a roundel is a cluster name, the dial reads tokens per second), and leave an unknown result as a ruled blank.
Do give every looping or entrance animation a still end state and honour reduced motion.
donts: Don't use gradients, box shadows, text shadows, glows or blur. The build has none.
Don't introduce a colour outside the four inks and two stocks, or tint one with transparency to make a panel.
Don't round the corners of buttons, inputs, frames or images. Circles belong to roundels, seals, dials, wheels and the menu's marker ring.
Don't set a fifth weight or a sixth face; four of the five faces have one weight, and emphasis is a change of voice.
Don't let the script or a stamp cover the letters of a headline; it crosses the baseline and carries a ground-colour stroke.
Don't place yellow, green or salmon as a card inside a buff page; an ink takes the whole page or stays inside a plate.
Don't sweep the needle or ease anything with bounce; the instrument steps and the press slides home once.
Don't use photographs, raster textures or icon fonts; marks and plates are drawn in the inks.
